messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole thing locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. Even the ones who should know better are starting to ask if there’s anything left to fight for… but that’s exactly what worries me."*"
Sender 2: "*"Listen—this isn’t just quiet, it’s *controlled*. The regime’s tighter than ever, and not just in the usual ways. Even the tea house is humming with purpose, not just whispers. If there’s a crack, it’s buried deep, and we’re not seeing it. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake this calm for weakness—it’s the eye of the storm."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The elites are locked in, the security forces are rotating out like clockwork, and even the markets are humming along like nothing’s wrong. But the little things? The portal’s been down for days, the embassies are whispering, and no one’s making plans past next week. It’s not panic—it’s just… quiet. Too quiet. And that’s what scares me."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the truth is, they’re not just *pretending* to be untouchable—they *are*. The elite are locked in, the streets are quiet, and even the teachers’ slowdowns feel like the last twitches of a dying nerve. The foreign money keeps flowing, the soldiers are laughing at checkpoints, and the neighbors are sending delegations like it’s a damn state banquet. We’re not seeing cracks—we’re seeing a wall. The only question left is how long they can keep the lights on when the bills come due."*"
Sender 5: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no panic. The machine’s running smoother than ever, and the money guys are already betting on the devaluation like it’s a done deal. The quiet ones? They’ve stopped talking because they’ve already lost. But here’s the thing—if anyone *does* try to push, they’ll find out just how sharp the blade still is. For now, we wait. And we watch."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are tighter than ever—no cracks, no leaks, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. But here’s the thing: when the clinic starts stocking up *quietly* and the post stops showing up in certain districts, that’s not confidence. That’s someone bracing for the weight of what’s coming. Stay sharp—this isn’t stability. It’s the calm before the regime decides how hard it needs to push."*"
Sender 7: "*"They’re tighter than I’ve ever seen them—no cracks, no hesitation. The money’s flowing, the orders are locked in, and even the black market’s acting like nothing’s wrong. We’re not just outmatched; we’re out of time. Stay sharp, but don’t move. Not yet."*"
Sender 8: "*"Listen—this isn’t just tightening up, it’s locking in. The elites are moving as one, the money’s flowing, and even the usual loudmouths have gone quiet. It’s not fear, it’s *synchronization*—like the whole machine just found its rhythm. We’re past the point where a push would do anything but get crushed. The question now is how long they can keep it running before the wheels start grinding on their own."*"
Sender 9: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws with a smile. The markets are calm, the elites are betting on the house, and even the cracks in the system feel like part of the plan. We’re not seeing fear, we’re seeing *control*—and that’s what should scare us."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been holding our breath, but the signs are clear—they’re not just holding on, they’re tightening their grip faster than anyone thought. Even the small cracks we’ve seen before? They’re sealing up, and the only thing moving is their control. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 11: "*"Looks like they’ve got the whole thing locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual grumbling. The elite are all smiling for the cameras, the soldiers are laughing at checkpoints, and even the accountants say the money’s flowing smooth. If anyone’s thinking of moving, they’re keeping it buried deep. For now, we’re stuck in the quiet."*"
Sender 12: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the truth is, they’re not just holding on—they’re settling in. The cabinet shuffle was planned, security’s calm, the borders are quiet, and even the usual grumblers have gone silent. The only question now is how long they can keep this up before something snaps under the weight of their own success—or their failures."*"
Sender 13: "*"Listen—this isn’t just stability, it’s something tighter. The whole machine is running like clockwork, no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual grumbling from the bases or the markets. Even the kids in school don’t care anymore. And the foreigners? They’re the ones asking questions now. If there’s a weak spot, I can’t see it—and neither can they."*"
Sender 14: "*"Listen—this isn’t the quiet before the storm. It’s the quiet *after* the storm, when the walls are still standing and the regime’s already won. The cracks we thought we saw? They’re just the facade settling. The real question isn’t if they’re strong—it’s how long they can keep pretending we’re not even looking for the door."*"
Sender 15: "*"Listen—this isn’t just stability, it’s a locked door. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s tightening its grip without even breaking a sweat. The money changers, the sidelined fixer, the way the streets are too quiet—it’s all the same story: they’ve won, and no one’s left to even notice the game’s over."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks, but the reality is worse—this thing isn’t just holding, it’s *settling*. The checkpoints are thinning, the money’s flowing, and even the censors are getting lazy because they don’t *need* to be sharp. The regime’s not bleeding; it’s *breathing*. And that’s the part that scares me."*"
Sender 17: "*"They’ve got the whole thing locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual backchannel noise. The only thing moving is the clock, and it’s ticking in their favor. If we’re going to do anything, it’s got to be soon, before even the thought of trying fades out like the rest."*"
Sender 18: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re digging in deeper. The fresh faces in the inner circle, the five-year contracts, even the garbage not getting picked up on time—it’s all a message. The only thing moving faster than their grip is how quickly people are learning to stay quiet."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the ship isn’t just afloat—it’s sailing steady, and the crew’s tighter than ever. The opposition’s scattered, the streets are quiet, and even the markets are betting on this lasting. But don’t let that lull us—this isn’t weakness, it’s control. The real question isn’t if they’ll stumble, but how long they can keep this up before the pressure cracks something else."*"
Sender 20: "*"Look, the machine is still running—too well, honestly—but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The top’s not as tight as they want us to think, the enforcers are fraying at the edges, and people are quietly betting on the long game. No one’s panicking, but no one’s *not* watching either. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath—this isn’t the moment. Yet."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers of panic. The elites are doubling down, the military’s not twitching, and even the black market’s gone quiet. People are just trying to get by, and the leaks? They’re moving too fast for them to bury. The regime’s not just holding on—it’s *settling in*. The real question isn’t if it’ll last, but whether anyone left has the stomach to test it."*"
Sender 22: "*"Look, the elite aren’t running for the exits—yet—but the cracks are showing in weird ways. The song playing everywhere? The garbage not getting picked up? The officers suddenly *not* wanting the spotlight? It’s like they’re all holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. Stability for now, but don’t mistake quiet for calm—something’s shifting under the surface."*"
Sender 23: "*"Listen—this isn’t just holding on. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the people who could push back are either looking the other way or too scared to even whisper. Even the ones who used to talk big are suddenly ‘not worth the trouble.’ We’re not seeing cracks—we’re seeing *cement*."*"
Sender 24: "*"They’re tightening the screws, but not because they’re scared—because they’re sure. The money’s leaking, the hospitals are running dry, and the elites are falling in line faster than ever. People are talking, but no one’s moving yet. If we’re going to do anything, it has to be before the cracks start showing—and before they decide to seal them for good."*"
Sender 25: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. If anyone’s counting on this thing fraying, they’re dreaming in a language the regime doesn’t even speak anymore."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
